voiceNote: Voice guide: first person, confident, warm, plain-spoken. Short sentences. Real numbers only — never invent results. Lead with the thinking, land on the craft. Copy stays close to Nicole's own writing.

siteSettings.heroLine: Nine years leading visual identity, creative campaigns, and marketing design — from strategic brief to final asset. Consumer brands, with a soft spot for health, wellness, and lifestyle.

about.headline: I work across the full creative arc — from strategic brief to production to final asset.
about.bio:
I'm Nicole — a Senior Designer and Brand Strategist with nine years of experience leading visual identity, creative campaigns, and marketing design.

My background is in consumer brands, with a growing focus on health, wellness, and lifestyle. I've been the sole in-house designer for a multi-location pet-wellness retailer, co-founded and designed a podcast brand that grew past 40,000 streams, and built brand systems that hold up across everything from packaging to a 75-location credentialing program.

The work I love most sits at the bridge between marketing and design: taking what a brand knows about its audience and turning it into creative that actually moves people — then sweating the details all the way to the shelf, the feed, or the screen.

experience.summary: Sole in-house designer for a multi-location pet-wellness retailer — brand creative end-to-end across campaigns, email, social, packaging, web, signage, and merch.
Co-founded a podcast brand; designed the full visual identity, template system, and website. Grew to 40K+ streams.
Brand identities, logos, social systems, and motion for startups including Loop, Straight Shot Post Production, and Neon Cheetah.
In-house designer across the full product and marketing ecosystem — packaging, social, stop motion, advertising, and new product development.

recognition: Graphis Design Award, Silver (2021) — Roosevelt brand identity & packaging
BFA Graphic Design, Maryland Institute College of Art (MICA)

projects.title: Let's Talk, Peaches
projects.intro: I co-founded Let's Talk, Peaches and designed the whole thing — the visual identity, a graphic template system that kept every episode on-brand, and the website. Along the way I art-directed episode graphics for some genuinely brilliant guests, and the show grew past 40,000 streams.

projects.title: Independent Pet Partners
projects.intro: Independent Pet Partners is a multi-brand, holistic pet-wellness retailer operating across the US. As the sole in-house designer, I own brand creative end-to-end — digital campaigns, email, social, packaging, web, signage, and merch — averaging 40 emails and 10 campaigns a month.

extraBlocks.heading: Ask Us Anything
extraBlocks.body: I art-directed a full 360° brand campaign from brief to production: built the mood boards, contributed to the shot list, and directed video and photography teams on set — dog talent included. The campaign delivered a multi-cut brand video (:30 / :15 / :06) running across Meta and Instagram, plus a proprietary image library shot in our own stores that replaced stock photography across every channel.

extraBlocks.heading: Systems, not one-offs
extraBlocks.body:
Beyond campaigns, I build the scaffolding that keeps a multi-brand retailer consistent: company-wide brand guidelines, a loyalty program identity, and a multi-level credentialing program enabling consistent brand expression across 75 locations. I also designed the wireframes and page mockups for a full website redesign, handing improved UX to the dev team.

The Roosevelt house brand — identity, packaging, and window displays — earned a Graphis Design Award (Silver, 2021).

projects.title: Ubbi
projects.intro: Ubbi is a baby and lifestyle brand. As an in-house designer I worked across the full product and marketing ecosystem — new product development, packaging design, social content, stop-motion production, and advertising. It's where I learned how design works as both a commercial and storytelling tool inside a product-led brand.

projects.title: Loop
projects.intro: Loop is an app that helps people manage personal challenges and anxieties through live audio experiences. I established the brand identity for Loop's social presence, then built a set of templates and motion assets so the team could keep publishing without losing the thread.

projects.title: Neon Cheetah
projects.intro: Neon Cheetah is a fashion blog committed to helping readers find confidence — their inner cheetah — through inspiration and fashion expression. With that mission in mind, I developed a brand identity bold enough to keep up with it.

projects.title: Cookie Dough Confections
projects.intro: The summer of 2017 I interned at Cookie Dough Confections, an edible cookie dough shop in NYC. Over two months I designed holiday packaging, a partnership label, and retail materials that had to look as good as the dough tasted.

projects.title: Get Your ____ Together
projects.intro: A 150-page, hand-bound, participatory book designed to help people lead more fulfilling lives. Readers flip, rip, spin, and write in the book to uncover its contents — a design that only finishes when someone actually uses it.

projects.title: Custom Lettering
projects.intro: I have a special place in my heart for handlettering — experimenting with different pens, brushes, and styles. There's something about the personal touch it brings to a project that no typeface quite replaces.

projects.title: Urban Outfitters
projects.intro: Product design iterations for Urban Outfitters' fall 2018 season, designed under both femme and bohemian style directions.

projects.title: Party Depot
projects.intro: While rebranding Party Depot, I was determined to kick the cliché party-store aesthetic. The new identity expresses the excitement of hosting while staying organized, bold, and modern.

projects.title: Motion
projects.intro: A few of my favorite motion pieces, most cut in After Effects — stop motion, logo animation, a lyric video, and quote animations.

projects.title: Cup Shop
projects.intro: Cup Shop is a collection of ready-for-retail coffee mugs, each inspired by a different kind of coffee lover, presented through a visual system of posters, a lookbook, and a website.
